item.title: Global investors remain bullish on China's long-term prospects
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
XIAMEN, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- A supersized market, growing innovation capacity, and policy predictability are creating long-term opportunities and sharpening China's appeal to global investors, said business leaders attending the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade. The fair opened Tuesday in Xiamen, east China's Fujian Province, drawing registrations from more than 1,200 government institutions and business delegations from 129 countries and regions, as well as 30 international organizations. Its permanent theme is "Expanding Two-Way Investment, Jointly Facilitating Global Development." This year's fair features Finland and Saudi Arabia as dual Guest-of-Honor countries for the first time. "China's rapid development has brought abundant opportunities for Finnish enterprises," said Sakari Puisto, minister of economic affairs of Finland. More than 250 Finnish companies and their subsidiaries currently have a presence in China. "We look forward to concluding multiple business cooperation deals during this visit," said Puisto. That confidence was reflected in both long-standing participation at the fair and plans for further investment in China. This year marks the 23rd consecutive time that AmCham South China has sent a delegation to the fair. The chamber represents more than 2,300 member enterprises, including globally renowned multinationals such as Nike, Johnson & Johnson and Pepsi, and its members account for 40 percent of the total volume of U.S.-China bilateral business, trade and investment. Over the past 23 years, its member companies have signed new investment agreements worth an average of about 2 billion U.S. dollars each year at the fair. "China remains a hot destination for investment," said Harley Seyedin, president of AmCham South China. Citing the chamber's 2026 Special Report on the State of Business in South China, Seyedin said 75 percent of enterprises plan to reinvest in China this year. Member companies are expected to reinvest 13.79 billion dollars in profits generated in China over the next three to five years. "This is undoubtedly a strong vote of confidence in the resilience and development potential of the Chinese market," Seyedin added. Data from China's Ministry of Commerce also point to continued foreign investment activity. Nearly 4,800 foreign-funded enterprises made additional investments in China in the first half of 2026. More than 37,700 new foreign-funded enterprises were established in the first seven months, up 4.4 percent year on year, while foreign investment in high-tech industries surged 32.7 percent. Stephen Phillips, founder and chief executive of CC Global Horizons Limited, said investors see high-potential growth opportunities in many areas of the Chinese economy. China has made great progress in areas such as life science, robotics and renewable energy, he said, adding that Chinese companies with advanced technologies could help other countries address pressing challenges. Pointing to China's five-year plans, Phillips said the world is highly unpredictable, yet China stands out for its predictability. "Consistent policy signals from China deliver a sense of certainty to investors," he added. Masaharu Nakayama, executive officer of Panasonic Holdings Corporation Group, said that China's ability to innovate and roll out AI applications, paired with Panasonic's technological expertise and global network, together with emerging growth areas like the silver economy, creates tremendous opportunities. "In our industry, China is among the world's fastest-evolving and most competitive markets. Products forged in this demanding market are globally competitive," he said. "We are delegating more authority to our Chinese entities and ramping up R&D investment, aiming to bring products, technologies and business models refined in China to the rest of the world." Nan Li Collins, director of the Division on Investment and Enterprise at UN Trade and Development and head of the World Investment Forum, said that China remains a major source and destination of international investment because of the scale of its market, manufacturing capabilities, skilled workforce, technological capacity, and integrated supply chains. "China's continued opening-up, together with its efforts to foster fair competition, improve the business environment, support innovation and advance the green and digital transitions, can create further opportunities for domestic and international investors," she said. Seyedin also voiced confidence in the long-term prospects of doing business in China, saying that view is widely shared among the chamber's members, which regard China as a preferred destination for long-term investment. "The future is bright, and we will remain part of China's economy for a very long time to come," Seyedin said. ■

item.title: Portraits | Faces of China's educators
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
BEIJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- China has an 18.7 million-strong teaching force, the backbone of the world's largest education system. Among them are those who have long served in rural areas, teachers who have made enduring contributions to scientific research, and educators who have crossed mountains and seas to bring knowledge overseas. On the occasion of the 42nd Teachers' Day, we present these faces of dedication, paying tribute to every Chinese educator whose dedication lights up budding dreams. Across China's vast rural landscape, rural teachers illuminate classrooms and light up the path of knowledge for children in the most remote communities. They take root at the podium, toil in obscurity, and achieve extraordinary feats at ordinary posts. On university podiums and at the frontiers of research, educators who do more than pass on knowledge pioneer innovation in the pursuit of the unknown. They stress the significance of talent cultivation and encourage young people to tackle cutting-edge challenges, guiding the nation's march toward scientific and technological strength. From across the country, wave after wave of educators have answered the call to teach in the far western reaches of Xinjiang and on the snowy plateau of Xizang. Some have stayed for decades, some have moved their entire families westward, tapping into their wealth of experience to boost educational quality in the western regions. “Go where your country needs you the most.” Around the world, Chinese educators are building bridges of mutual understanding, respect and appreciation. Whether in mountain classrooms in Sri Lanka, or in agricultural laboratories in Ethiopia, they share knowledge across borders, ranging from language and medicine to technology and beyond. From cities to rural areas, from preschool to lifelong learning, the faces of educators extend far beyond these pages. The warm embrace of a special education teacher, the skilled hands of a vocational instructor, the patient companionship of a kindergarten teacher... Their daily perseverance upholds the future of every child. We cannot capture every face, but every act of dedication deserves to be remembered.

item.title: Advanced technology boosts conservation, restoration of Terracotta Warriors in NW China's Shaanxi
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
Restoration specialists piece together a terracotta warrior at the on-site conservation lab of the Pit No.1 of the Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Sept. 3, 2026. At the world-famous Terracotta Warriors site in Xi'an, visitors can now witness a once behind-the-scenes process -- experts meticulously restoring over 2,000-year-old clay soldiers. At the newly launched conservation lab in Pit No. 1, specialists piece fragmented pottery together manually, reviving scattered relics into solemn and life-size warriors. The lab officially opened in 2024, celebrating the 50th anniversary of the discovery and excavation of the iconic Terracotta Warriors. A professional excavation and preservation facility in Pit No. 2 was also completed and put into operation. The two facilities form a full-cycle conservation system covering excavation, transportation, restoration and storage. This advanced system greatly improves the protection of the warriors' original pigments. Buried underground for over 2,000 years, the Terracotta Warriors suffered severe damage from fires, soil collapses and underground water fluctuations, with most original colors fading away over time. Previously, surviving paint layer would easily curl, peel or flake off once exposed to drastic environmental changes after excavation. Today, newly unearthed painted relics are directly transferred to the on-site lab. Through keeping stable humidity control, ultrasonic inspection, 3D scanning, professional cleaning and reinforcement treatment, researchers now do their utmost to preserve the warriors' ancient original hues. item.title: China-initiated international alliance to combat telecom, cyber fraud established
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
NANJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- An international alliance aimed at countering cross-border telecom and cyber fraud was established on Thursday. Representatives from 46 founding countries, 34 observer countries and four international organizations, including the United Nations and Interpol, attended the inaugural conference in Lianyungang in eastern China. Initiated by the Chinese government, this alliance is an intergovernmental organization designed to promote cooperation among law enforcement agencies in tackling transnational telecom and cyber fraud and related crimes. Representatives from China and other founding members, such as Vietnam, Laos, Kenya, Cambodia, Pakistan and Russia, addressed the conference, while a representative from Interpol delivered a congratulatory message. Participants welcomed China's initiative to establish the International Alliance Combating Telecom and Cyber Fraud and recognized its significance in safeguarding global public security. Participants issued a joint statement on the alliance's establishment, saying telecom and cyber fraud has become a global challenge requiring stronger international cooperation. According to the statement, establishing a more focused, professional, efficient and action-oriented intergovernmental organization based on international conventions will help coordinate efforts to combat telecom and cyber fraud and related crimes, and protect the security and legitimate rights and interests of individuals, legal entities and other organizations. The alliance was formed amid growing global concerns over cyber-enabled fraud. A report by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime estimated that such fraud had caused losses of between 18 billion U.S. dollars and 37 billion U.S. dollars in Southeast Asia alone in 2023, with many schemes linked to organized criminal groups operating across borders. China has in recent years strengthened law enforcement cooperation with over 30 countries, including Spain, the United Arab Emirates and Myanmar, to tackle cross-border telecom and cyber fraud, developing cooperation mechanisms and achieving results in joint efforts against these crimes. Since 2023, China and Myanmar have carried out joint operations that led to the dismantling of four major criminal gangs in Myanmar's Kokang region. Earlier this year, police authorities from China, the United States and the United Arab Emirates conducted their first joint law enforcement operation, resulting in the arrest of 276 suspects. Cooperation with Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka and other countries has also led to the arrest and repatriation of more than 20,000 telecom and online fraud suspects this year. The alliance also reflects China's efforts to translate the Global Security Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative into concrete actions. Put forward in 2022 and 2025, respectively, these two initiatives emphasize the importance of addressing global challenges via cooperation and improving global governance. ■

item.title: China sees continued growth in foreign cross-border travel
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-10
NANJING, Sept. 10 (Xinhua) -- Foreign travel to China continued to pick up in the first eight months of this year, as the country expanded visa-free access and other measures aimed at making entry easier for international travelers. Foreign nationals made nearly 61.29 million trips across China's borders from January through August, up 19.5 percent over the year-earlier level, according to data released Thursday. Of the entries into China by foreign nationals during the period, 23.72 million were visa-free, accounting for 77.6 percent of the total, up 26.8 percent year on year. The figures were released at a sub-forum on immigration management cooperation held as part of the 2026 Conference of Global Public Security Cooperation Forum, held in the city of Lianyungang, east China's Jiangsu Province. China has steadily eased visa rules to allow longer stays and wider travel for international visitors, part of efforts to facilitate cross-border exchanges and boost inbound tourism. It currently offers unilateral visa-free entry to nationals of 50 countries, while its 240-hour visa-free transit program covers 57 countries. ■

item.title: Hong Kong, Macao students interact with Shenzhou-23 crew from orbit
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and students pose for photos during a live space lecture of the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 9, 2026. (Photo by Lui Sui Wai/Xinhua) HONG KONG, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- The "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session was held simultaneously in Hong Kong and Macao on Wednesday morning, as the three Chinese astronauts of the Shenzhou-23 crew currently carrying out a manned space mission at the Tiangong space station delivered a live space lecture for students. Shenzhou-23 mission commander Zhu Yangzhu, astronaut Zhang Zhiyuan and Hong Kong's first payload specialist Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, delivered an engaging and vivid science lesson to the young people of Hong Kong and Macao. The event was jointly organized by the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) government, the Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) government and the China Manned Space Agency, with the main classroom set up at Lai's alma mater, Tsuen Wan Public Ho Chuen Yiu Memorial College in Hong Kong. A total of 160 Hong Kong students and 50 Macao students attended the main venue in person, joined by school principals, teachers, youth representatives, and tech professionals from both cities. The HKSAR government and the Macao SAR government also arranged for teachers and students of primary and secondary schools to watch the live broadcast simultaneously on campus. During the session, the three astronauts demonstrated scientific experiments in the unique space environment in real time and shared glimpses of daily life aboard the space station. They conducted a series of science demonstrations, including baking a cake in the space kitchen, wringing out a wet towel, and tending the space vegetable garden. Lai also showcased the operating procedures for MUSICO, a lightweight, high-resolution, high-precision carbon dioxide and methane point-source detector developed under the leadership of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Throughout the lecture, the astronauts answered questions from students on space science and astronaut life in orbit. John Lee, HKSAR's chief executive, asked Lai whether she had received the letters sent by the students. In response, Lai said she had read through every letter from home, pledging to honor their trust and spare no effort to complete her in-orbit mission. She added that her spaceflight reflected the country's strong support for Hong Kong. Kong Chi Meng, director of the Education and Youth Development Bureau of the Macao SAR government, said that the lecture was not only a vivid lesson in science and technology education, but also a profound lesson in patriotism, with the three astronauts serving as exemplary role models for students. ■ John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), and students attend a live space lecture of the "Tiangong Class" Hong Kong and Macao Designated Session in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 9, 2026. item.title: Xi extends Teachers' Day greetings, urges nurturing capable youth for national rejuvenation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-09
BEIJING, Sept. 9 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has extended greetings to teachers and educators across the country ahead of Teachers' Day, which is celebrated annually on Sept. 10. In a congratulatory message, Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called on teachers nationwide to enhance their professional competence and capabilities, and foster a new generation of young people to shoulder the mission of realizing national rejuvenation. Over long periods of time, teachers across the country have devoted themselves to education, imparting knowledge and nurturing young minds, said Xi, commending their significant contributions to the cause of the Party and the state. Xi emphasized the importance of carrying out the basic task of fostering virtue through education and cultivating a high standard of professional integrity and conduct on the new journey. He also called for fostering public respect for educators, encouraging support for education, and bringing together all efforts to make China a leading country in education. China boasts the largest education system in the world, having roughly 440,000 schools at all levels and of all types, with 280 million students and 18.7 million teachers. ■
